document.abstract: Summary.—According to this writer the new factor in the talkies is sound for its own sake and not speech, speech having found its place long ago in the printed captions of silent films. Study of these old subtitles, it is said, quickly defines screen dialog, while pure sound, no longer confused with spoken words, becomes a great artistic force. It was explained when presented, that this paper was really a chapter in “The Talkies,” an immediately forthcoming book. Its appearance here is with the express permission of the author and of the publishers, Henry Holt & Company, of New York.
